analysis: What changed vs Thursday's 9am brief: (1) the defensive rotation stuck - Dow +1.08%, S&P +0.33%, but the week still reads negative for tech (Nasdaq -2.4%, S&P -0.9%); Asia rebounded overnight and futures are flat-to-up, so the bounce has not failed yet. (2) The Roadster demo flipped TSLA from -1.3% Thursday to +4.6% premarket - the biggest single-name overnight move in the brief's universe, and it is pure event sentiment ahead of Oct 21 earnings. (3) CoreWeave's CDS record (1,194.5 bps, >60% implied default probability) is the dominant credit signal; Huang's defense moved the stock (+5.94% close) but not the bonds - the equity/credit divergence is widening, and premarket -2.5% suggests the stock relief is leaking. (4) The Fed corner clarified without moving: Warsh's non-hawkish dodge took October hike odds to 15%, and Saturday's blackout means today's industrial production data has no Fed cushion. (5) USAC's routine distribution is the only fresh name-specific news in the coverage set. Verification note: an InvestorsHub/advfn item claiming a public 'NASDAQ:ANTP' Anthropic ticker is wrong - Anthropic remains private with no ticker - so it was dropped. Signal vs noise: CRWV credit, the haven bid, and the rotation's breadth (8 of 11 sectors green, equal-weight +1.37%) are the signal; the Roadster spectacle and the after-hours earnings moves are contained noise.

community_signals.takeaway: 580-comment overnight thread (403 points): the engineering crowd split between awe at the thruster demo and skepticism - the 'hopping, not flying' legality/safety debate dominates. Tape takeaway: the demo landed as spectacle, not product.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a steady-to-slightly-higher open Friday: S&P 500 futures +0.1%, Dow +0.2%, Nasdaq 100 ~flat (WSJ, ~3am PT), after Thursday's defensive rotation - S&P 500 +0.33% to 7,744.06, Dow +1.08% (+556) to 52,177.69, Nasdaq +0.08% to 26,713.03. Asia rebounded overnight: Kospi +2.05% after a 7.6% plunge, Nikkei +1.8%, Taiex +0.55%, Stoxx 600 +0.3%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rotation held overnight and Asia stabilized, but with the S&P -0.9% and Nasdaq -2.4% on the week (Investopedia), Friday is about whether the bounce has follow-through or just marks a pause before the open.

headlines.headline: Tesla unveiled the redesigned second-generation Roadster at SpaceX's McGregor, TX test site Thursday evening: cold-gas thrusters developed with SpaceX powered an uncrewed demo that drove upside down on a curved ramp, flipped ~21 feet in the air and 'kick-flipped' over the full Tesla lineup. Tesla claimed a 0.81-second 0-60 in the demo, >230 mph top speed and 300+ mile range; production targeted for 2028. Three configs: Performance ($50K deposit, <1.6s), Thrust ($250K deposit, <0.9s) and invitation-only Rocket (<0.59s, not road-approved). TSLA was +4.59% at $379.08 in premarket trade (~4:45am ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: Event-driven halo bounce - +4.6% premarket prices the spectacle, not unit economics; with no final price announced and road legality unclear, the pop is sentiment that can reverse into the Oct 21 earnings print.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave's 5Y CDS hit a record 1,194.5 bps Thursday (ICE Data Services) - pricing a >60% five-year default probability - while its 2032 9.625% notes traded ~76.5-80 cents on the dollar with yields past 16%; Oracle CDS also hit records (Bloomberg, The Times). Jensen Huang said Nvidia needs no backstop and 'cost of capital is actually decreasing'; the stock still reversed from -9.5% intraday to close +5.94% at $69.69, and Deutsche Bank kept a buy. Friday premarket: CRWV -2.5% (WSJ).
headlines.why_it_matters: The equity bounce vs the bond-market distress pricing is the tape's central tension - credit keeps screaming default while the stock rallies on Huang's words; premarket -2.5% says skepticism won the night.

headlines.headline: Chips fell again Thursday: the SOX closed -0.88% for its seventh straight down day (intraday -4%+), NVDA -1.84%, Dell -6.9%, HPE -7.1%. TSMC reported a 68.7% profit jump but its shares declined anyway. Broadcom's and Intel's CEOs both called capital shortage - not chips - the biggest AI bottleneck; reportedly ~$745B of hyperscaler AI capex this year (single-source estimate), with Alphabet posting negative free cash flow for the first time.
headlines.why_it_matters: A record TSMC print could not stop the bleed - financing, not demand, is the sorting variable now, and the server/equipment leg extends the stress from cloud balance sheets into future capex.

headlines.headline: Apple posted its first-ever close above a $5T market cap on Wednesday (Dow Jones Market Data) - only Nvidia had been there before - after a ~25% 2026 rally on AI-capex restraint and premium pricing; Thursday AAPL -0.28%. The rest of the megacaps were mixed Thursday: MSFT +1.08%, GOOGL +0.45%, AMZN +0.27%, META -0.11%. Meta launched Muse Spark Open, an 816B MoE coding model (single-source, unverified by major outlets).
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple's $5T close is the other side of the AI trade - rewarded for capex restraint while spenders get sold; that divergence is the positioning question for the rest of the week.

headlines.headline: Fed Chair Warsh, in a Bangkok fireside chat with IMF's Kristalina Georgieva, refused to pre-judge the Oct 27-28 or December meetings - 'It's a new chapter at the Fed, and we're not in that business anymore' - stressing data dependence after hot CPI and PPI prints. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid: the most important thing was what he didn't say; markets took the lack of hawkishness as good news. CME Oct hike odds fell to 15% from 28%; December at 89%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Warsh's non-hawkish dodge is the last scheduled Fed word before Saturday's blackout - with industrial production and trade prices out today, the data stands alone from here.

headlines.headline: After the close Thursday: J.B. Hunt Q3 EPS $1.82 - a beat on the lowered $1.81 consensus but well under the $2.09 pre-warning level (CFO Brad Delco had guided down 5-10% vs Q2); revenue $3.68B beat $3.57B; diesel 'north of $6' a gallon; shares fell ~2-4% after hours. Interactive Brokers Q3 adjusted EPS 67c vs 68c est (miss), revenue $1.91B vs $1.87B (beat); -1% after hours. Alcoa EPS $1.82 vs $1.51 est (beat), revenue $3.70B vs $3.77B (miss). Varonis +2% after hours: Proofpoint to acquire it in a ~$6.3B all-cash deal closing H1 2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: Freight and brokerage prints are economy read-throughs - JBHT's diesel-cost squeeze is the inflation pass-through story - while the Varonis takeout says M&A still clears in a down tape.

usac.headline: USA Compression (TXSE: USAC) declared its Q3 2026 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized), payable Nov 6 to unitholders of record Oct 26 (BusinessWire, Oct 15). Q3 results drop before the open Tuesday, Nov 3; investor call at 11am ET (10am CT).
usac.why_it_matters: Routine distribution declaration - no change signal; the next catalyst is the Nov 3 Q3 print. Carried forward: Oct 1 8-K (34.47M Class A units at $26.7206, 9.25% fixed, non-convertible, non-redeemable, to J-W Energy); TXSE listing since Oct 5; Q2 beat ($0.31 EPS vs $0.28 est, $342.15M revenue vs $340.49M est); $600M 6.75% notes due 2035; consensus Hold, $29.50 target.
